items.label: fc02-crash-window
items.front: Why does the architecture critique call the JSON persistence crash-unsafe, and what is the standard fix?
items.back: WriteAllUnsafeAsync does File.Create over the live file, so a crash mid-serialize truncates the whole dataset; the fix is write-to-temp-file then atomic rename (and eventually a real database).

items.label: fc03-secret-based-authz
items.front: What is the precise name for the pastebin's edit/delete protection model, and what does it NOT give you?
items.back: Authorization by possession of a shared secret (the delete key, checked by hash). It is not authentication: nobody is identified, there are no accounts, and brute-force attempts are not rate-limited.

items.label: fc01-read-side-effect
items.front: Pastebin clone: name the hidden side effect of a successful GET by slug.
items.back: GetAsync increments ViewCount, sets LastViewedAt, and rewrites all of pastes.json under the store gate - a read is a full-file write, which matters for crash windows and disk churn.

items.prompt: In ResolveExpiry, what do PasteExpiration.Never and an unrecognized enum value each produce?

choices.text: Never gives a null ExpiresAt; the fallback arm quietly assigns one day
Never gives DateTimeOffset.MaxValue; unknown values throw an exception
Both reach the default arm, so each of those pastes lives for one day
Never is rejected during validation; unknown values get a null expiry

choices: Never gives a null ExpiresAt; the fallback arm quietly assigns one day
Never gives DateTimeOffset.MaxValue; unknown values throw an exception
Both reach the default arm, so each of those pastes lives for one day
Never is rejected during validation; unknown values get a null expiry

items.explanation: The switch maps OneHour/OneDay/OneWeek to offsets, Never to null, and `_ => now.AddDays(1)` as a silent default. (Unknown values normally never reach it: Validate() checks Enum.IsDefined.)

items.prompt: How does the store persist the delete key a creator chooses?

choices.text: With bcrypt and a per-paste salt, tuned to verify slowly
As an unsalted, hex-encoded SHA-256 hash of the key
In plaintext in pastes.json, since the file is local
It is not stored - it is checked against a value kept in memory

choices: With bcrypt and a per-paste salt, tuned to verify slowly
As an unsalted, hex-encoded SHA-256 hash of the key
In plaintext in pastes.json, since the file is local
It is not stored - it is checked against a value kept in memory

items.explanation: HashDeleteKey = Convert.ToHexString(SHA256.HashData(UTF8(deleteKey))); the raw key never reaches pastes.json. It avoids raw storage, but it is a fast unsalted hash, not a password-grade KDF.

items.prompt: A PUT /api/pastes/{slug} arrives with a well-formed body but the wrong delete key. What does the API return?

choices.text: 404 with one blended message, same as a missing or expired paste
400 Bad Request, because Validate() rejects keys that do not match
401 Unauthorized, since the delete key is the authentication credential
403 Forbidden, with a field error naming the DeleteKey property

choices: 404 with one blended message, same as a missing or expired paste
400 Bad Request, because Validate() rejects keys that do not match
401 Unauthorized, since the delete key is the authentication credential
403 Forbidden, with a field error naming the DeleteKey property

items.explanation: A wrong key is deliberately indistinguishable from a missing or expired paste. UpdateAsync returns null for not-found, expired, and wrong-key alike, and the endpoint maps null to Results.NotFound("Paste not found, expired, or delete key is incorrect.") - the guide calls out that auth errors are not distinguishable.

items.prompt: A paste expired an hour ago but is still physically present in pastes.json. The caller holds the correct delete key. Which mutation can still succeed?

choices.text: PUT alone - an update renews the expiry, while deleting expired pastes fails
Both - mutations skip the expiry check as long as the delete key matches
DELETE alone - its guard checks existence and the key hash, not expiry
Neither - both of them call IsExpired before they touch the record

choices: PUT alone - an update renews the expiry, while deleting expired pastes fails
Both - mutations skip the expiry check as long as the delete key matches
DELETE alone - its guard checks existence and the key hash, not expiry
Neither - both of them call IsExpired before they touch the record

items.explanation: UpdateAsync refuses expired pastes: its guard is `paste is null || paste.IsExpired(...) || DeleteKeyHash != ...`. DeleteAsync's guard omits the IsExpired clause, so an expired-but-unpurged paste is still deletable.

items.prompt: What does GET /api/pastes/search?q=a return, and how would the search behave if that guard were removed?

choices.text: 400 ProblemDetails; without it, the store's own check still returns 200 []
400 ProblemDetails; without it, each call scans every unexpired public paste
200 with the 20 newest public pastes, since a tiny filter matches them all
404, because search is routed per slug and 'a' is not a known paste slug

choices: 400 ProblemDetails; without it, the store's own check still returns 200 []
400 ProblemDetails; without it, each call scans every unexpired public paste
200 with the 20 newest public pastes, since a tiny filter matches them all
404, because search is routed per slug and 'a' is not a known paste slug

items.explanation: The endpoint rejects queries shorter than 2 chars (after trim) with BadRequest. The guard is defence in depth: SearchPublicAsync repeats the check (PasteStore.cs:158-162) and returns [] before taking the gate or reading the file, so without the endpoint guard q=a would answer 200 with an empty array and scan nothing. The full linear scan (Contains(OrdinalIgnoreCase) over title, content and language of every unexpired public paste) costs queries of 2+ characters - the risk register's 'Search full scan' latency risk. (Item corrected in the rebalance-2 fix pass: the key used to claim the removed guard would let 1-char queries scan every paste.)

items.prompt: A client issues GET /api/pastes/{slug} for an existing, unexpired paste. Besides returning the paste, what does PasteStore.GetAsync do?

choices.text: Appends a view event to a separate analytics log, leaving the paste as is
Bumps ViewCount and LastViewedAt, then rewrites the whole pastes.json file
Bumps ViewCount in memory, persisted later by the next create or update
No side effects - GetAsync is a pure read that just deserializes the file

choices: Appends a view event to a separate analytics log, leaving the paste as is
Bumps ViewCount and LastViewedAt, then rewrites the whole pastes.json file
Bumps ViewCount in memory, persisted later by the next create or update
No side effects - GetAsync is a pure read that just deserializes the file

items.explanation: Every successful read is also a disk write: GetAsync builds `updated = paste with { ViewCount = paste.ViewCount + 1, LastViewedAt = ... }`, swaps it into the list and calls WriteAllUnsafeAsync - so reads mutate and persist state.

items.prompt: Two POST /api/pastes requests land at the same instant on one server process. What stops them from corrupting pastes.json, and where does that protection end?

choices.text: No protection - concurrent creates in one process routinely lose a paste
Optimistic concurrency: a write retries when UpdatedAt changed underneath it
The OS file lock taken by File.OpenRead blocks the second request until done
One SemaphoreSlim(1,1) serializes store operations, but only within one process

choices: No protection - concurrent creates in one process routinely lose a paste
Optimistic concurrency: a write retries when UpdatedAt changed underneath it
The OS file lock taken by File.OpenRead blocks the second request until done
One SemaphoreSlim(1,1) serializes store operations, but only within one process

items.explanation: Every public method does `await _gate.WaitAsync()` around read-modify-write of the whole file. The lock is process-local, so a second deployed instance could still interleave writes; the risk register flags exactly this: process-local lock only, race under multi-instance.

items.prompt: When is an expired paste physically removed from pastes.json?

choices.text: On the first read that notices the expiry, which deletes it before returning
Right when its ExpiresAt instant passes, removed by a background timer
It stays on disk indefinitely and is merely hidden from queries and reads
On the next write of any kind, which filters out expired pastes before saving

choices: On the first read that notices the expiry, which deletes it before returning
Right when its ExpiresAt instant passes, removed by a background timer
It stays on disk indefinitely and is merely hidden from queries and reads
On the next write of any kind, which filters out expired pastes before saving

items.explanation: Purging piggybacks on unrelated operations. There is no scheduler; WriteAllUnsafeAsync keeps only `!p.IsExpired(now)` entries whenever anything saves the file. Reads filter but do not remove (GetAsync returns null yet still leaves the record).

items.prompt: The 8-character slug is drawn from a 57-character alphabet. Which characters were deliberately left out, and why?

choices.text: Hyphen and underscore, which would break the route's matching
Uppercase letters, so slugs stay valid in case-insensitive URLs
The vowels, so that random slugs do not spell out real words
l, I, O, 0 and 1 - the look-alikes that people easily misread

choices: Hyphen and underscore, which would break the route's matching
Uppercase letters, so slugs stay valid in case-insensitive URLs
The vowels, so that random slugs do not spell out real words
l, I, O, 0 and 1 - the look-alikes that people easily misread

items.explanation: RandomToken's alphabet is abcdefghijk(m)nopqrstuvwxyz / ABCDEFGH(J)KLMN(P)QRSTUVWXYZ / 23456789 - 25 + 24 + 8 = 57 characters: lowercase l, uppercase I and O, and digits 0 and 1 are missing so humans cannot misread a slug. (Prompt corrected from '58-character' in the quiz rebalance: the alphabet string has 57 characters.)

items.prompt: Slugs mix upper- and lowercase letters, yet SlugEquals uses StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase everywhere. What follows?

choices.text: Lookups become case-sensitive but creation is not, so duplicates get minted
abC234xy and ABc234XY name the same paste, shrinking the effective namespace
Lookups are unaffected - the comparison matters just when new slugs are made
The store lowercases each slug before saving it, so the mixed case is lost

choices: Lookups become case-sensitive but creation is not, so duplicates get minted
abC234xy and ABc234XY name the same paste, shrinking the effective namespace
Lookups are unaffected - the comparison matters just when new slugs are made
The store lowercases each slug before saving it, so the mixed case is lost

items.explanation: Every lookup (get, update, delete) and the CreateUniqueSlugAsync collision loop go through SlugEquals, which ignores case - uniqueness is enforced case-insensitively, so mixed-case output does not multiply the address space.
